Russian Casualties in 2026 Top 300,000, Ukraine Says — Russia has lost an estimated 301,030 service members killed or wounded since the beginning of 2026, Ukraine’s General Staff said. More than 124,000 of those casualties occurred during June, July and August, while Russia’s estimated personnel losses since the full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1.51 million.

WWII Podcast to Which Putin Should Have Listened — Listeners to the UK-based WWII podcast “We have ways of making you talk” can see that Vladimir Putin, the self-avowed student of history, has ironically failed to identify that his disastrous invasion of Ukraine has repeated many of the same missteps that led to the failure of Operation Barbarossa – Hitler’s 1941 invasion of the USSR.

EXPLAINED: Energy Truce in Ukraine – Third Time’s the Charm? — Trump said Monday that Kyiv and Moscow agreed to an energy truce – Kyiv says yes but only if others can guarantee an actual and lasting truce, while Moscow has stayed quiet. Previous attempts suggest that clear terms are needed to impose an actual ceasefire – and only if the parties are willing to.

‘We Have Something to Say’: Lavrov Says Russia Is Ready to Resume Ukraine Talks — Russia is signaling openness to renewed Ukraine talks, with Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov saying Moscow “has something to say.” Meanwhile, Trump’s claimed energy truce remains unconfirmed, as Kyiv demands reciprocity and Moscow calls the proposal a “good initiative.”

Ukraine Launches ‘Vivaldi’ Counteroffensive in Donetsk as Russian Forces Face Setbacks Near Lyman — Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps has launched the ‘Vivaldi’ offensive in Donetsk, targeting Russian infiltration tactics. Biletsky reported territorial gains and heavy Russian losses, while Russian milbloggers acknowledge setbacks and OSINT analysts estimate Russia lost 200-240 sq. km (77-93 sq. miles).

54% of Eastern Germans Say Weapons for Ukraine Are Excessive, Poll Finds — Eastern Germany is increasingly skeptical of military support for Ukraine, with 54% of respondents calling Berlin’s weapons deliveries excessive, compared with 39% in the west, a new ARD-Deutschlandtrend poll shows. The findings come as the far-right AfD gains ground in eastern Germany.

‘Warsaw Will Disappear in 2 or 3 Days’: Kremlin Threatens Poland — Kremlin aide Nikolai Patrushev claimed Polish statehood would cease to exist within “two or three days” if Warsaw entered a military conflict with Russia. His remarks followed Sikorski’s warning that NATO’s overwhelming air superiority would allow it to defeat Russia quickly in the event of an attack.

Intel Reveals 19 Russian Missile, Drone Firms Still Outside International Sanctions — Ukraine’s military intelligence agency said 19 companies connected to Russia’s KRET radio-electronics holding remain outside all international sanctions lists. The companies produce components for Iskander and Zircon missiles, military drones, fighter jets, helicopters, and electronic warfare systems.

EXPLAINED: Zelensky’s Headaches Increase as Prosecutor General Flees Ukraine — Prosecutor General Kravchenko, who found himself at the epicenter of a corruption scandal, left Ukraine together with his wife and sent notices of suspicion to the heads of the anti-corruption bodies that were investigating people close to him.

Russian Frigate Fires Flares at Danish Military Helicopter in International Waters — A Russian warship in international waters off the coast of Denmark fired flares at a Danish Air Force Fennec helicopter engaged in routine photographic surveillance of the vessel, according to the Danish Armed Forces Command. No further details of the incident have yet been released.

Putin Resists Energy Truce Announced by Trump — Russian President Vladimir Putin is reluctant to agree to a reciprocal halt in attacks on Ukrainian and Russian energy infrastructure before winter, people familiar with Kremlin thinking told the FT. The report undercuts Donald Trump’s claim that both sides had already accepted a truce, which surprised Kyiv, and came without public guarantees from Moscow.

‘VOICES. An Evening of Premieres’: Kyiv Camerata to Present Music of Memory, Hope and Victory — “VOICES. An Evening of Premieres” will bring together Ukrainian and American music by Nico Muhly, Hanna Havrylets, Victoria Poleva, Volodymyr Zubytskyi, and Zoltan Almashi, moving from memory and loss to hope and victory.

US Midterms: Trump’s 5,000-Dollar-Per-Adult Pledge — Trump’s proposed $5,000 “dividend” for every adult US citizen has drawn criticism across Europe. Newspapers question its financing, warning it could sharply increase US debt and deficits. Commentators also accuse Trump of vote-buying, highlighting inflation and economic costs, while arguing that cash-based politics is increasingly undermining democracy in the US and elsewhere.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Refinery, Drone Plant and Ozon Facility in Massive Overnight Attack — Ukraine launched a major drone and missile attack on Russia, reportedly hitting a Rosneft refinery and other facilities. The strikes came as Moscow and Kyiv resumed talks on an energy ceasefire, though Putin reportedly opposes a deal before winter.

Battle for Belarus — Belarus remains a strategic pressure point in Russia’s war on Ukraine, with Alexander Lukashenko balancing dependence on Moscow against domestic opposition to joining the conflict. Meanwhile, China’s economic and diplomatic support gives Belarus limited room to resist deeper Russian control, as Ukraine views a possible future where Belarus separates from Moscow as essential for good-neighborly relations.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Gas Stations, Kill 1 as 200 UAVs Attack Ukraine — Russian forces launched 200 drones at Ukraine overnight, including Shahed-type and jet-powered UAVs. Air defenses downed or suppressed 187, while strikes hit seven locations and two gas stations in Kyiv, killing one and wounding 7.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 14, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 14, 2026.

NATO Jets Shoot Down Drone Over Lithuania — NATO fighter jets destroyed a drone over Lithuania in the latest security incident along the alliance’s eastern flank, while Poland launched preventive aviation operations during renewed Russian attacks on Ukraine.

Zelensky Seeks Reciprocity as US Urges Halt to Strikes on Russian Energy — Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to halt strikes on critical infrastructure if Russia genuinely reciprocates, as the US pushes for restraint and Congress advances tougher sanctions on Moscow.

‘I Will Go Back to Ukraine at the Next Opportunity’ – Dan Fried After Russian Train Strike — Daniel Fried told Kyiv Post that Russia’s strike near the Polish border was designed to intimidate Ukraine’s Western backers, but said it would not deter them from returning to the country.

Kim Jong Un Calls Russia’s War ‘Sacred,’ Pledges Continued Support for Moscow — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un reaffirmed support for Russia’s war against Ukraine in a letter to Vladimir Putin, calling it “sacred” as reports point to possible additional North Korean troop deployments.

Putin-Linked Russian Businessman Paid in Part for Trump Jr.’s Wedding Celebrations — Trump Jr. and Bettina Trump confirmed that Russian businessman Umar Kremlev, who received Russia’s Order of Friendship from President Vladimir Putin in April, paid for two nights of their wedding celebrations.

Merz Vows Continued Support for Ukraine as Pro-Russian AfD Secures Victory — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Monday, Sept. 14 that Berlin will maintain military support for Ukraine despite the rise of the far-right, pro-Russian Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. His pledge follows the AfD’s nearly 44% in Saxony-Anhalt, where the party campaigned to restore relations with Moscow.

SBU Urges Residents of Occupied Ukrainian Territories Not to Participate in Russia’s September Elections — The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) has urged residents of occupied territories not to take part in Russia’s planned Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections, calling it illegal. Organizing or promoting the process may carry criminal liability, as the vote may try to legitimize Russia’s occupation.

World Bank to Send Ukraine $841 Million Under Canadian Guarantee — Ukraine's Finance Ministry said it will soon receive $841 million from the World Bank under a guarantee from the Government of Canada, with the funds earmarked to cover pension payments in the state budget. The disbursement falls under the Tenth Additional Financing of the World Bank's PEACE in Ukraine project, which will reach a total of $54.3 billion, the largest investment project in the World Bank's history.

Koretskyi: Ukraine Risks Losing $29.5B in Aid Without Urgent Parliamentary Votes — Ukraine reportedly risks losing a substantial amount of $29.5 billion in planned international financing if the parliament misses deadlines for required legislation, according to Ukraine’s prime minister. The government has moved its deadline for 42 required decisions to Oct. 15 as it prepares for winter pressure on the budget, defense needs and energy system.

Ex-CIA Chief: Inside Putin’s Mafia State — Former CIA Chief of Station Sean Wiswesser tells Kyiv Post’s Jason Jay Smart that Russia’s FSB, SVR and GRU are far from the polished spy services of myth – they’re corrupt, often sloppy, yet still lethal abroad. From Skripal’s poisoning to assassin Vadim Krasikov’s triumphant return home, Wiswesser traces a system that rewards aggression and rarely punishes failure, blending mafia-style extortion, cybercrime and disposable Telegram-recruited operatives

Anthropic Disrupted Russian Attempt to Develop Autonomous Drone Swarms — Anthropic, the AI safety and research company said that it had prevented Russian developers from using its Claude coding agent to create software to power the Kremlin’s autonomous kamikaze drones. The system was designed to select and attack targets, including individuals, without the need for operator intervention.

EU Extends Russia Sanctions for 7 Days Amid Dispute Over Delistings — EU member states extended sanctions tied to Russia’s war in Ukraine for another seven days on Monday, Sept. 14. A renewed vote, scheduled for Sept. 22, comes as the EU ambassadors previously failed to agree on the removal of Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov and Alfa Bank co-founder Mikhail Fridman from the list.

Zelensky Hits Former Press Secretary Iuliia Mendel With 10-Year Sanctions — Zelensky imposed 10-year sanctions on former press secretary Mendel and nine Russian citizens. The move follows Mendel’s controversial May interview with Tucker Carlson, in which she made several claims about Zelensky and the war.

Trump Claims Ukraine, Russia Agreed to Halt Energy Infrastructure Strikes — US President Donald Trump said Monday, Sept. 14, that Ukraine and Russia agreed not to strike each other’s energy infrastructure. While Kyiv has not confirmed the reported arrangement, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv would reciprocate only if its allies could guarantee a halt to Russian strikes.

Zelensky Signs a Decree Ousting Kravchenko as Prosecutor General — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree ousting Ruslan Kravchenko from his post as Prosecutor General on Monday, Sept. 14. The decision came amid the “Carthage” probe into alleged protection of fraudulent call centers within the Prosecutor General’s Office and a widening conflict with anti-corruption agencies.

Sikorsky Slams Nawrocki Team Over Ukraine Envoy — Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorsky rebuked President Karol Nawrocki’s office after it suggested Piotr Lukasiewicz might not be approved as ambassador to Ukraine. Sikorsky argued that the president cannot reject candidates endorsed by parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, while Nawrocki’s spokesman raised concerns about Lukasiewicz’s record.

China, India, Turkey Remain Top Buyers of Russian Fossil Fuels — In August, China remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, followed by India and Turkey. The EU remains the fourth-largest buyer of Russian energy, despite purchasing the least Russian LNG since 2022.

Kremlin Vows to Keep Striking Ukraine After Russian Attack Near Polish Border — The Kremlin said Russia will continue striking targets across Ukraine after a Russian attack hit a railway locomotive just 2 km from the Polish border. Poland called the incident an escalation, while NATO and the EU vowed continued support for Kyiv.

Ukrainian F-16s Shoot Down Jet Drones – But Is It Enough? — Zelensky says Ukraine has resorted to costly AIM-9s and AIM-120s air-to-air missiles from Ukrainian F-16s to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones as Canada pledges new packages. The Ukrainian Air Force says pilots also used the 20mm cannon at times, but questions remain whether Ukraine has enough ammunition to shoot down thousands of jet-powered drones, AIM-120s or not.

‘Our Victory or Defeat’: Ukrainian Top Commander Reveals What Could Force Russia to Reconsider the War — Third Army Corps commander Andriy Biletsky said Ukraine’s success will depend on defending its skies from ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones this winter. According to him, if Russia fails to capture Donbas or break Ukraine’s resilience, Moscow could face a fundamental decision about continuing the war by March or April 2027.

Two Milchakovs, One Rumor: Confusion Over Which Russian Commander Died — Partisan group says Russian Gen. Sergey Milchakov was likely killed in a Ukrainian strike on a Donetsk headquarters. The claim has not been confirmed, while Russian media disputed separate reports that "Rusich" commander Alexei Milchakov had been killed.

Trump Calls on Ukraine to Lay Off Energy Industry Strikes on Russia — Trump urged Zelensky to stop striking Russian diesel facilities and blamed Ukraine for global fuel shortages. The US leader’s demand followed record August attacks and almost daily drone strikes against Russia, with Ukraine hitting refineries and igniting fires visible from space.

Europe Prepares for War as Germany Sends Up to 1,000 New Troops — Germany will add postings to its permanent brigade in Lithuania this fall, with up to 1,000 active-duty soldiers potentially affected, Bild reported. Berlin plans to station 4,800 troops on NATO’s eastern flank by the end of 2027 but has filled only about 60% of the required positions with volunteers.

Ukraine Sees Exponential Growth in Private Security Firms Providing Anti-Drone Protection — In November last year Ukraine’s Defense Ministry unveiled a project to allow private businesses to defend their own plants against Russian aerial attacks. Now more than 50 enterprises have obtained permits to use licensed security firms or their own trained staff to supplement the country’s national air-defense network.

Russian Drones Just Miss Former CIA Director David Petraeus: a View From a Train Near the Polish Border — Kyiv Post presents an eyewitness account of the attack on a train at the Polish border that nearly hit former CIA Director David Petraeus and came on the heels of ex-UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s departure.

Ukraine Has Leverage Over Trump Now — Timothy Ash argues that President Trump cannot blame Ukraine alone for rising energy prices, saying his Iran policy and decision to reduce US support for Kyiv helped push Ukraine toward developing its own long-range strike capabilities and gave it greater leverage over Washington.

‘The Battlefield Has Gone Underground’: Khartiia Commander Reveals Ukraine’s Edge Over Russia — The commander of Ukraine’s 2nd Khartiia Corps said the battlefield in his sector has shifted underground, where Ukrainian troops are operating more effectively than Russian forces. He also urged Ukraine and its Western partners to develop short-range missiles against Russia’s jet-powered drones.

Ukraine Must Attack Russia’s Missile Plants to Win War, MITS Capital CEO Says — MITS Capital co-founder and CEO Perry Boyle told Kyiv’s Yalta European Strategy Forum that air defense alone cannot save Ukraine and urged partners to back attacks on Russia’s missile-production plants. He also criticized weak foreign investment in Ukraine’s defense sector. Budget Committee Chair Roksolana Pidlasa echoed his call to focus on defeating Russia.

Russian Attack on Pryluky Kills 3, Wounds 7 — Three people were killed and seven injured when Russian forces attacked an agricultural enterprise in central Pryluky, Chernihiv region. At least two explosions were recorded, damaging windows in nearby apartment buildings, while police warned residents to avoid the area because of the threat of another attack.

Russia Launches Kalibr Cruise Missiles Directly From Base, Ukraine Says — Ukraine’s navy said Russia has been launching the naval-based Kalibr missiles directly from port, instead of sending the warships out at sea, for four months in a row. Russia also reportedly has four vessels capable of launching the missile left in the Black Sea, with cruise missile launches relatively rare in recent months.

Kharkiv Holds First Pride March Since Russia’s Full-Scale Invasion — KharkivPride held its first march on foot since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, with about 200 people following a 500-meter underground route. Participants called for legal recognition of same-sex partnerships, stronger hate-crime legislation, and greater attention to equality and civilian safety.

‘Fully Surrounded’: Russian Forces Suffer Major Defeat in Donbas — Ukraine’s counteroffensive has reportedly reversed Russia’s gains since March and disrupted Moscow’s plan to encircle Sloviansk and Kramatorsk from the north.

Germany Plans €3.4B Tomahawk Missile Purchase — Germany’s Defense Ministry plans to earmark nearly €3.4 billion for US-made Tomahawk cruise missiles and mobile Typhon launchers, POLITICO reported. The acquisition would give the Bundeswehr its first ground-based long-range strike capability, though the amount may change and the purchase still requires budgetary and parliamentary approval.

Ukraine May Get License for Older, Less Advanced Patriot Missiles — US President Donald Trump said Washington is discussing a license to allow Ukraine to manufacture a less advanced version of its Patriot interceptor missiles. The proposal appears to revive a plan Trump announced in July but later questioned on grounds of “security.” US officials also warned that setting up production would take years and would not ease Kyiv’s immediate air-defense shortages.

Canada Considers Joining EU €90 Billion Ukraine Loan — Canada is negotiating participation in the European Union’s €90 billion loan for Ukraine, which will finance Kyiv’s budgetary and defense needs in 2026 and 2027. The talks come as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks closer ties with Europe and aims to reduce Canada’s dependence on the United States.

Ukraine’s EU Membership Path Faces New Risk as Outgoing Prosecutor General Targets NABU — Ruslan Kravchenko’s resignation and subsequent announcement of a case against NABU’s director have renewed scrutiny of Ukraine’s EU reform commitments. Judicial reform advocate Mykhailo Zhernakov says the next prosecutor general’s selection must involve international experts, while parliament must restore safeguards in judicial appointments.

Exclusive: Poland’s FM Radek Sikorski Comments for Kyiv Post — Poland’s FM said Russia’s new jet-powered drones pose a threat that requires action from both Ukraine and its allies. Speaking at the YES Conference in Kyiv, he also praised Ukraine’s resilience and reaffirmed Poland’s solidarity with Kyiv.

Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Leaves Country Amid Anti-Corruption Showdown — Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko reportedly left the country overnight in an official vehicle, amid an escalating clash with anti-corruption agencies and now involving President Volodymyr Zelensky. His departure came hours after he accused NABU chief Semen Kryvonos of crimes, prompting the president to call for the chief prosecutor’s dismissal.

Why ‘Sanctioning Russia Act’ Is Putin’s Biggest Nightmare — If the US House of Representatives passes the “Sanctioning Russia Act,” which mandates a 100% maximum tariff on the five largest countries buying Russian oil and gas and punishes countries helping Russia evade sanctions, it could be game over for the Russian economy.

Polish FM: ‘We Would Defeat Russia Quite Quickly’ if Moscow Attacked NATO — Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said NATO has “overwhelming superiority” in air power and could defeat Russia “quite quickly” if Moscow attacked, adding that Europe could destroy Russia’s remaining refining capacity in weeks.

Ukraine Faces New Russian Jet-Powered Drones | Stefan Korshak — Ukraine Brief on TVP World is joined by Stefan Korshak, Senior Defense Correspondent at the Kyiv Post, to discuss the escalating attacks and Ukraine’s air-defense challenges. While Ukraine can intercept many conventional drones and ballistic missiles, faster jet-powered Geran drones are creating increasingly difficult threats.

So You Want to Be a MilTech Millionaire? — Ukraine is rapidly becoming a major player in military techology. Now foreign defense manufacturers are flooding into the country to take advantage of the opportunity to test and develop products in actual battle conditions. Here are some of the pitfalls to be aware of on both sides.

Poland Scrambles Security Chiefs After Russian Strike Near Border With Ukraine — Poland’s prime minister convened an emergency security meeting after a Russian strike hit a Kyiv-Warsaw train near the Ukrainian border, as Donald Tusk warned Moscow’s escalating actions could eventually threaten Polish territory.

Trump Tells Zelensky to Stop ‘Knocking Out Diesel Fuel in Russia’ — Trump urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to stop striking diesel fuel facilities in Russia, warning that other targets should be pursued instead. Ukraine’s attacks on Russian energy infrastructure have disrupted fuel production and contributed to domestic shortages. Trump says peace efforts are progressing, but Poland’s foreign minister remains skeptical as Russia maintains its war objectives.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 13, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 13, 2026.

Why Boris Johnson? Putin’s Long-Running Grudge in Focus After Train Strike — A near-miss Russian drone strike at Yahodyn station has cast fresh light on Vladimir Putin’s long-running hostility toward Boris Johnson. The former British prime minister has stood near the top of the Kremlin’s list of Western adversaries because of his early and outspoken support for Ukraine’s defense.

Russian Drone Strike Narrowly Misses Boris Johnson, Carl Bildt and Ex-CIA Chief David Petraeus — Ukraine and Poland say the Russian drone strike near the border may have been aimed at the diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson and other senior Western officials, which had passed through Yahodyn shortly before the attack.

Amid Air Raid Sirens and Shelter Shows, Ukrainian Fashion Week ‘Unbreakable’ — In Kyiv, Ukrainian Fashion Week's Spring/Summer 2027 season pressed on through a week of daytime Russian strikes, moving three runway shows into a bomb shelter. Designers and organizers called Russian attacks the most disruptive yet, but the season closed on a high, with designer Oleksandra Sakhaudinova winning the Grand Prix for "Reclaiming the Light."

Russian Hackers Used Claude AI to Target Ukraine — Threat groups linked to Russian intelligence services used Anthropic’s Claude AI tool to execute multi-victim cyber campaigns targeting Ukrainian and Western institutions, according to a threat intelligence report by Anthropic. A Visit to a Unique Porcelain Museum in Kyiv — The Kyiv Porcelain Museum is a unique institution that continues to operate despite the war. It showcases numerous rare and highly valuable porcelain pieces from a variety of manufacturers while introducing visitors to the history and artistry of porcelain. The museum is headed by our colleague, Oleksandr Shvets, who is also its founder and owner.

Keeping the Bridges Open — Moscow’s attacks are turning the Dnipro river into a daily barrier between the city’s two halves. But there are fears not only for Kyiv’s physical bridges, with the need to also maintain social bonds across Ukraine, especially as winter approaches and hopes for peace recede.

Meloni Rules Out Alliances With Opponents of Ukraine Aid — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni rejected speculation that she could form political coalitions with parties opposed to military aid for Ukraine, saying that she will not abandon her principles for electoral advantage ahead of elections next year. Her comments deliver a sharp warning to far-right politician Roberto Vannacci, an outspoken critic of arms deliveries to Kyiv who has gained momentum in domestic polls.

Germany Weighs Restricting NATO Defense Plans if AfD Governs — German defense officials are considering steps to block regional state governments from accessing confidential national and NATO defense plans if the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) enters government. Italian Ex-Foreign Minister Giulio Terzi: Italy Is Unequivocally on Ukraine’s Side — There can be no doubt that Feb. 24, 2022 was a watershed. Since then, security, deterrence and defense against the tangible threat of extremely serious military aggression have once again become central concerns.

Sikorski Urges Aggressive NATO Drills Near Kaliningrad — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski argued that NATO should conduct aggressive military exercises near Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave to exploit Moscow’s localized vulnerabilities and force Vladimir Putin to redeploy troops away from Ukraine. Sikorski noted that Kaliningrad currently holds “practically no troops” because the Kremlin assumes NATO will not act, suggesting decisive allied maneuvers would inject strategic ambiguity.

Russia’s ‘Beacon’ for Sick Children, Facing Jail for Pro-Peace Message — Prominent Russian charity leader and children’s hospice founder Lida Moniava has been placed under supervised curfew and fitted with an ankle monitor pending trial on charges of spreading “false information” about the Russian army. Putin’s Economic Growth Claims Diverge From IMF Data — Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed at the BRICS summit in New Delhi that Russia’s economy expanded 10.3% from 2023 to 2025, outpacing global benchmarks despite 30,000 sanctions, while alleging an 8% drop in EU industrial output. IMF data shows global economic growth reached 10.7% over the same timeframe, while Eurostat records an EU industrial decline of just 0.6%.

Russian Strike in Kramatorsk Kills 2, Wounds 4 — A Russian strike targeted a civilian car moving through the center of Kramatorsk in Donetsk region on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, killing two people and injuring four others, according to Donetsk Regional Military Administration Head Vadym Filashkin. Emergency services deployed to the scene as authorities worked to determine the full extent of the damage. Filashkin condemned the deliberate assault on civilians and renewed urgent appeals for resident

Sweden Votes in Election Thriller, far Right Eyes Govt Role — Sweden began voting on Sunday, Sept. 13, in a closely contested general election that will determine whether the far-right enters government for the first time or the left-wing opposition reclaims power. Opposition leader Magdalena Andersson of the Social Democrats warned against a cabinet dominated by the Sweden Democrats, while conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson campaigned on law-and-order gains, pledging ministerial posts

Territory Remains Main Obstacle to Ukraine-Russia Deal, Kushner Says — US special envoy Jared Kushner stated at the YES 2026 conference in Kyiv that territorial disputes remain the chief obstacle preventing a peace agreement between Ukraine and Russia. Kushner explained that while Vladimir Putin outlined Moscow’s territorial demands, Ukraine firmly refuses to retreat, leaving mediators to craft a creative formula that satisfies Kyiv while compelling Russia to end hostilities. China Threatens to Cancel US Summit Over Taiwan Arms — China warned the US that it intends to cancel a planned leaders’ summit this month if Washington approves new arms transfers to Taiwan beforehand, Kyodo reported. Beijing reiterated that the status of Taiwan remains an inviolable “red line,” following heightened friction after Donald Trump previously described arms sales as a “bargaining chip”.

Russia Faces Shortage of Chinese Drone Jet Engines — Russian forces are facing disruptions in supplies of Chinese-manufactured jet engines for long-range strike drones due to coordinated measures by Ukraine and international partners, HUR Deputy Head Vadym Skibitsky said. Peace Through Strength NOW! — Over 700 leaders, diplomats, and veterans from 28 countries convened in Kyiv for the 22nd Annual Meeting of the Yalta European Strategy (YES), held Sept. 11-12 under the motto “Peace Through Strength NOW!” Organized by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation, the forum focused on accelerating military aid, expanding defense manufacturing, and reinforcing air defense ahead of winter.
